posts.cooked: 4.  In case it matters, what's the exact timing on resolving the actions listed on both sides of a villain character card?  Let's say I'm playing against Grand Warlord Voss on Advanced, and he's on his Super-Warrior form side.  First you check to see if there multiple minions in play; if so, he flips to Conquering Alien form.  Since he's no longer on his Super-Warrior form, he doesn't deal damage or play a villain card, right?  Conversely, if there were somehow 10 minions in play at the start of Super-Warrior's turn, he'd flip to Conqueror form, then immediately score an Overrun victory?  If there were somehow both 0 and 2 minions in play, despite this being obviously impossible, would he just keep flipping himself back and forth as he unsuccessfully tries to get to the end of his card without hitting a trigger?

4. Correct, since he has flipped, once he gets to his end of turn phase he will no longer do anything that was on his previous side.

That is is a bit of an odd question, But yes he would constantly flip.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: The same is true of Wraith's Stun Bolt and Nightmist's Investigation (and probably some other stuff I forgot). If an action is dependent on your needing to do damage (or discard a card, or whatever), the phrase "If you do..." is usually there (eg Unity destroying equipment to put out bots). If you need to have taken damage, you'll see something like "If you take damage this way..." (eg the Adept's Polyphoric Flare).

Envisioner wrote:
2.  Can an Incapacitated Hero perform a "skip the rest of your turn to do X" action, for the sake of an Environment clause or the like?  
As a follow-up to this...I know incap heroes can skip their turns and etc...but there are cards that allow heroes to discard or overturn cards to get rid of themselves (lots of enviroments do this), do incap characters count for discard/overturn?  Based on the fact that incap heroes have turns and still contribute to H, but not cards in play, I would guess that the conditions have not been met, so that card would not destroy itself, and that heroes would have to use normal destruction effects to get rid of those cards instead of the conditions on that card that allows self-destruct.  Pillars of Hercules (Ruins of Atlantis) is one of those cards I'm thinking, but I'm sure there's others, like Blighted Streets (Rook City environment) and others I can't recall at this time.

Pillars of Hercules is a "skip your turn" card, so I don't think is an example like you're looking for.  Blighted Streets says " At the end of each hero's turn, if that hero dealt no damage this turn, their player may discard 2 cards to destroy this card."  An incapacitated hero has no cards in hand, so cannot fulfill this.  (Nor could a hero with only one card in hand at the end of their turn.)  I forget which card, but one of them allows you to discard your hand to get rid of the card.  For that one, I would allow a hero with no cards in hand to discard their (empty) hand, but I would not allow an incapacitated hero to do it; I'm not sure I can justify that well.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
An incap hero not only has no cards in their hand, but they cease to have a hand at all. At least that is how I would phrase it.

And dpt, you can't choose to discard your hand if you have no hand to begin with, so a active hero with 0 cards in hand can not choose that option.

Think of it like Ra's ongoing that gets a +1 damage for every villain ongoing in play (I forget the name). If there are 0 villain ongoings in play and Ra has his staff, you can't use that power to deal 0+1=1 damage (as that 0 signifies that there is no damage to modify with the staff in the first place).
